question_text: Find the value(s) of $k$ for which the graph of the quadratic function $y = kx^2 - (k - 6)x + (k - 6)$:

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting $\Delta > 0$ and noting $k \ne 0$ for a quadratic function

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A quadratic graph cuts the $x$-axis twice when its discriminant $\Delta > 0$ and the leading coefficient $a \ne 0$.
step_by_step:
Since the equation is a quadratic, $a 
e 0 \implies k 
e 0$. Hence, $-2 < k < 6, k 
e 0$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to exclude $k = 0$, which would make the function linear rather than quadratic.

subparts.solution:
The graph touches the $x$-axis if $\Delta = 0$.
$\therefore k = -2 \text{ or } k = 6$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A parabola touches the $x$-axis (has one repeated real root) if and only if $\Delta = 0$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Neglecting the negative sign or misidentifying roots as $+2$ and $-6$.

subparts.solution:
The graph misses the $x$-axis if $\Delta < 0$.
$\therefore k < -2 \text{ or } k > 6$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A quadratic graph misses the $x$-axis (no real roots) when $\Delta < 0$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Failing to reverse the inequality sign when dividing by $-3$.
